unit.why: A single tale: the Yehudi of Peshischa stays with the narrator's great-grandfather, a vodka-selling host, and repays him with business advice to buy calfskins, which then sell at double profit.

stories.end_quote: שהיהודי שילם שכר האכסניא שלו היטב
stories.summary_en: The Yehudi of Peshischa and his companions lodge for four weeks with the narrator's great-grandfather in Opatów, who stops selling vodka and feeds them despite his wife's worry. The Yehudi then advises him to buy calfskins on credit, and when the emperor orders boots for his army a merchant pays double, so the Yehudi has well repaid his lodging.
